evidence: Panel: `canRedo()` has no floor and the redo stack outlives store reconstruction. CodeRabbit: the floor should not be computed from `getUndoStackForTest()`. Changing the accessor adds no floor to `canRedo`.

panel.summary: `canRedo()` has no floor and the Yorkie redo stack survives store reconstruction, so a remount can offer a redo belonging to a previous store instance
panel.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:113 returns raw `doc.history.canRedo()`, while `undoFloor` is re-captured per instance at yorkie-note-store.ts:49. packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:93 constructs a NEW YorkieNoteStore whenever the effect re-runs (didMount/doc), reusing the same Yorkie Document — the redo stack from the prior instance is still there, so the toolbar (notes-toolbar.tsx:193 -> editor.canRedo()) can enable Redo and re-apply an edit the current session never undid.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::`canredo()` has no floor and the yorkie redo stack survives store reconstruction, so a remount can offer a redo belonging to a previous store instance

coderabbit.detail: **Avoid depending on `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` outside tests.** `Document.getUndoStackForTest()` is exposed in `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13, but its `ForTest` suffix indicates it is a test helper, not the stable public history API. Keeping the store’s `undoFloor` calculation tied to this helper makes application code brittle to future SDK changes.
